_comment: WC2026 QUARTER-FINAL (QF99: winner of Brazil-Norway vs winner of Mexico-England). KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets the Argentina-Switzerland winner in the semi-finals (M102). Nominal bracket orientation is Norway (home, feeder 93) vs England (away, feeder 94) on a neutral venue; modelled here with ENGLAND as home for clarity (the favourite) -- immaterial on a neutral venue; the web app flips the orientation. Routes: England WON Group L (4-2 Croatia, 0-0 Ghana, 2-0 Panama; rating 91), beat DR Congo 2-1 in the R32 (Kane brace, from 1-0 down) and won the 3-2 thriller vs host Mexico in the R16. KANE IS FIRING, but England CONCEDES in almost every game (2 Croatia, 1 Congo, 2 Mexico) -- a real attack with a leaky-ish defence. Norway finished 2nd in Group I (4-1 Iraq, 3-1 Senegal, 1-4 France; rating 81), won 2-1 vs Ivory Coast (93' winner) and then pulled the shock of the round: ELIMINATED BRAZIL 2-1 with a HAALAND BRACE from a 26% advancement position. Class gap ~10 (91 vs 81) -> England the clear favourite, BUT this is the BTTS rule's ELITE-STRIKER EXCEPTION in its purest form: (1) Norway has HAALAND, in red-hot form (brace vs Brazil) -- do NOT hard-trim (lambda 1.15, the same nuance that was vindicated vs Brazil); (2) England's defence is leaky (conceded in 4 of 5) -> Norway scores; (3) England's own games run HIGH (4-2, 2-1, 3-2 -- and the Mexico-England lesson: don't anchor a low total against England). -> an OPEN, higher-scoring tie: BTTS-YES 57%, Over 2.5 55%, xG 2.90. England favoured (their attack vs Norway's leaky GA-6 defence), but Norway's upset equity is REAL and at the UPPER end of its range (the Brazil-Norway lesson: an elite-striker underdog is where the favourite's ~35% elimination tail actually fires -- they have already done it once). Home = England (nominal; neutral venue; bracket shows Norway as home). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).
